correctness.rationale: The genus-one quotient discriminant and Hasse invariant are derived explicitly; the known degree-power-of-two Jacobian isogeny is prime to five. Smooth coefficients are counted using the discriminant (s²−4)(t²−4) and character sum −1. A single Hasse zero is counted using H_r+Δ=(s²+1)(t²+1), a paired intersection via r²=s² and a Möbius map excluding {0,3,4}, and triples via (a−2)²(a²−2a−2). Inclusion–exclusion proves the formulas for every q=5^n. Finite checker passed for q=5,25,125; finite tests are supporting evidence only.

value.rationale: This natural genus-three moduli family has three correlated elliptic Hasse loci; computing their complete simultaneous rank census over every extension is a structural arithmetic count, not an arbitrary finite sample. Characteristic-five parity changes the geometry of the rational Hasse-boundary intersections; the theorem exposes explicit q²-, q-, and finite-sized lower-rank strata, alongside Newton slopes and a-numbers. The all-extension formulas are not a routine substitution into a pre-existing table.
